title: Claude Code's 'Don't Ask Again' File Exposes Passwords and Keys in 1,122 Public Copies on GitHub
content:
Claude Code's 'Don't Ask Again' File Exposes Passwords and Keys in 1,122 Public Copies on GitHub (thehackernews.com) 21
			
		 	
				Be careful with the file .claude/settings.local.json, warns The Hacker News:
Passwords and API keys that developers typed into commands they approved in Claude Code are sitting in public GitHub repositories, where anyone can read them.  When a user selects "Yes, and don't ask again," Anthropic's AI coding assistant can save the command, word-for-word, including the secret, in a project settings file.  Software security company Apiiro said that 1,122 public copies of that file hold at least one secret, though it did not test whether any still work. One company the researchers notified earlier this week confirmed its key had been live...
Removing [the file] from a project does not undo the leak, because older versions stay in git history and in forks of the repository. The researchers' advice is to rotate first: change every password, token, and key the file has ever held, then clean up...
Claude Code tries to keep the file out of git. The first time it writes the file in a git repository, it adds the file to the user's global git excludes, its settings documentation says. Git on that computer then ignores the file in every repository.  That protection stays in one user's git settings on one computer. It does nothing for a file that was already committed, the researchers say. Claude Code never adds the file to the project's own .gitignore, so the protection does not travel with the project.  In 539 of the 1,105 repositories the researchers traced, a commit listing Claude as a co-author changed the file. They take this to mean Claude often commits the file itself.
Apiiro's search of public GitHub found 104,185 copies of the file in 103,617 repositories, its research write-up shows. About 1.1% of them, or 1,122 copies, hold at least one secret. Together they hold 1,379 different secrets... ]And "in half of those repositories it had been there for at least 217 days."]  More than a third of the secrets open a database directly, including 379 database passwords. Others include 43 SSH logins for public servers, 42 tokens for GitHub, GitLab and npm, and 23 AWS keys.  Among the owners of these files are 63 organizations, mostly software companies of all sizes. The strongest cases include a database vendor's own admin-level cloud key and the owner password of a medical-records database, the researchers say.  
Boris Cherny, Anthropic's head of Claude Code, responded to the story in a comment on Hacker News:
"Historically Claude Code has not done secret scrubbing (there are many good tools for that), but we are looking into what we can do to prevent this. 
That said, a few thoughts:
1. .claude/settings.local.json is meant to stay local. This is not a file you should check into source control. We automatically gitignore it when Claude creates the file, so in this case the files were manually created and checked in (docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings)
2. Permission rules are old hat. Everyone should be using auto mode instead. It is safer and also does not require manually maintaining finicky allow/deny lists. Auto mode is enabled by default and is included for free in all plans.
3. Regardless of what agent you use, you should have secret scanning enabled. GitHub and other source control hosts offer it. There are many threat models that it protects against and you should absolutely use it if you can. (see https://github.com/security/plans)" 
Cherny also named approaches Anthropic plans to prototype,  Apiiro notes in an update, citing Cherny's goal of
"making sure auto mode catches this, building in basic secret scanning," and, when a reader noted the same can happen in auto mode when it asks about a sensitive command, answered "good catch."
Claude Code users had already filed a bug report on the issue on August 11, 2025, notes The Hacker News, but "An automated bot closed that report as 'not planned' on January 3, after 60 days without activity."
Three more bug reports were then filed, according to the researchers.  "None got a reply from Anthropic, and three were closed automatically as inactive or duplicate."

report.summary: Claude Code 设置文件明文存密钥，1122 份已在 GitHub 公开泄露
report.background: Claude Code 的权限确认机制提供“Yes, and don't ask again”选项以减少重复授权，会把用户批准的命令原样写入项目下的 .claude/settings.local.json。这一设计提升了 agent 自主执行的流畅度，也让命令行中偶然出现的密码、token 被固化到磁盘。随着 AI 编程 agent 大规模进入日常开发，仓库里的各类配置文件正成为新的密钥泄露攻击面，而 git 的分布式特性使“删掉文件即修复”的直觉彻底失效。安全公司 Apiiro 的扫描把这一隐患从设计讨论变成了可量化的现实。
key_points: 在公开 GitHub 上扫描到 104,185 份该文件、分布在 103,617 个仓库；其中 1,122 份含至少一个密钥，合计 1,379 个不同密钥。
泄露内容很关键：超过三分之一的密钥可直接打开数据库，含 379 个数据库密码、23 个 AWS 密钥、42 个 GitHub/GitLab/npm token、43 个公网 SSH 登录。
Claude 常常自己提交这个文件：在 1,105 个被追踪仓库中，539 个是由 Claude 作为共同署名的提交改动的。
防护机制不随仓库传播：Anthropic 只把文件写进本机的全局 git excludes，从不写入项目的 .gitignore，换台机器或换个人就失去保护。
删除无效且响应迟缓：git 历史与 fork 长期留存，半数仓库里文件已存在至少 217 天；2025 年 8 月的 bug 报告被机器人以“not planned”关闭，后续三份无回复被自动关掉。
Anthropic Claude Code 负责人 Boris Cherny 承认历史上未做密钥清洗，称文件本应只留在本地，建议改用 auto mode 并开启 secret scanning，承诺后续内置扫描与自动拦截。
report.impact: 对 AI 行业，这意味着 agent 工具的默认行为必须按“随时可能泄密”来设计，权限缓存、命令日志与密钥清洗应成为基线能力，而不是可选插件。对开发者，凡是让 agent 记录命令的本地配置都要当作未来会公开的文件对待，仓库级的 secret scanning 与 push protection 应默认开启。对普通用户，风险最终落在所用产品的后端：某数据库厂商的管理员级云密钥、某医疗记录数据库的 owner 密码已在公开仓库里躺了数月，受影响企业需要立即审计历史提交并轮换凭证。
report.tools: 建议关注：GitHub Secret Scanning 与 Push Protection（服务端拦截）、gitleaks 与 TruffleHog（本地及历史提交扫描）、git filter-repo 与 BFG Repo-Cleaner（清理历史，务必先轮换密钥）；同时熟悉 Claude Code 的 auto mode 与 settings 文档，减少 hand-maintained 的 allow 列表。
